minutes.headline: Committee approved the school bus contract and opened school choice slots while the FY20 budget gap stayed open.
minutes.summary: Public comment mostly opposed cuts to French and student stipends. The committee heard the superintendent's entry report, reviewed its goals, approved a bus contract, school choice slots and a secretary negotiating representative, and gave final readings to two policies. The superintendent said the town's higher target still leaves a shortfall and that restoring cut positions would be reviewed for the next meeting.

what_happened.line: The School Committee approved the school bus transportation contract as presented; the minutes record the vote but not the tally.
The committee voted to open school choice slots for incoming freshmen and sophomores, on the superintendent's recommendation.
The FY20 school budget stayed unresolved: the town raised the target, but the schools remain short, and no vote was taken.
The superintendent and team are to recommend at the next meeting which cut positions and stipends to restore.
The committee appointed a member to the secretaries' negotiating team and gave third readings to policies 5400 and 5406.

why_it_matters: The FY20 school budget gap is still open, so French, activity stipends and teaching positions that residents raised in public comment could be restored or cut at the next meeting.

The bus contract drew only one bidder, the current vendor, and it rises over three years, so transportation is a cost that will be paid from the school budget, which the town budget, mostly taxes, funds.
